Commentary.Commentary: The players are back on the field. Sikandar Raza has his players in a huddle. He will hope that his words serve as an inspiration to his side. Right. off they disperse and out walk the Lankan openers - Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis. Richard Ngarava has the new ball in his hand. Nissanka to face. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...
Right then. 163 to win for Sri Lanka. Can Zimbabwe pull off a rabbit off the hat with a brilliant bowling display? The run chase is on our heels.

Time to don a hat to 'Wow'indu. With a limping leg, he managed to struck the chords right again, picking up three wickets. He mixed his lengths and pace really well, foxing the batters. Here he is, talking to the host broadcaster. Hasaranga says that due to a hamstring injury he missed the last ODI match but he is feeling good now. Continues that the wicket looks good, but dew might be an issue to the bowlers. Also adds that he batted well in ODIs, but he has to do the same in this format. Ends up reckoning that the bowlers have done well and believes that the batters will chase it down.

Decent bowling performance by Sri Lanka. The fast bowlers did not leak too many runs in the Powerplay and then, the spinners kept the batters in check in the middle overs. Impressive was the way they came back after the 61-run stand for the third wicket between Raza and Bennett. If any, the only question to be asked to Shanaka would be as to why didn't he give Kamindu Mendis the ball, with the pitch offering grip. Still, he would be happy with the way his side came back.

It was looking good in the middle overs with the runs coming on nicely, albeit not that quickly, but critically, wickets kept in hand. However, Bennett fell just a run before his half century and the scenario changed. Wickets kept on tumbling and eventually, Raza, getting stranded of partners, lost his wicket too. Somehow, his team huffed and puffed its way past the 160-mark.

Zimbabwe started off their innings briskly, with Brian Bennett off to a flier. They kept losing wickets but Bennett kept them in good stead, with the Powerplay score reading 43/2. Then came the skipper, Sikandar Raza, and alongwith Bennett, quickened the tempo.

A better batting display in terms of runs on the scoreboard by Zimbabwe but they will be disappointed once again. They had a good platform set at 101/2, but ended up scoring just 61 runs in their last 45 balls, for the loss of 6 wickets. There is some kind of a hold on the pitch but it will take a really magnanimous bowling effort to defend this total.

Very full, outside off, Graeme looks to squeeze it through the off side but gets it off the inner half of the bat towards square leg in the deep. Neither batter is interested in the second and ZIMBABWE END THEIR INNINGS ON 162/8.

Commentary.Commentary: The umpires take their places on the field. Out come the players from Sri Lanka behind them, spreading out onto the field. Additionally, this is the 50TH T20I TO BE PLAYED IN PAKISTAN. Right, now come the two openers from Zimbabwe - Brian Bennett and Tadiwanashe Marumani. It will be Nuwan Thushara to kick things off to Bennett first up. Here we go!

Time for the national anthems. It will be Zimbabwe's anthem to be sung first. Right, 'Apa Sri Lanka Namo Namo Matha' has also been sung and we are now and truly ready for Thursday's cricketing action to kick off in Pindi. Believe it or not, this is the FIRST T20I TRI-SERIES IN PAKISTAN! So this series already has a historic tag attached to it. Imagine what would happen if we actually see an upset taking place. In a normal world, for this match, Zimbabwe beating Sri Lanka would be considered an upset.

Historically, a Sri Lanka-Zimbabwe clash tends to invoke the feeling of a one-sided game, but recently, these two sides were involved in a compelling white-ball series in Zimbabwe, which did go in Sri Lanka's favour but not without the hosts giving a fight in almost every game. In fact, in the second T20I, the hosts blew away the Islanders for a paltry 80, which is the confidence they would be taking into this match.

KUSAL PERERA is up for a chat with the broadcasters. He mentions that he has played in the Pakistan Super League a few times, where the weather was quite chilly, but it's even colder now. Adds that he's been dealing with a right shoulder injury and is undergoing rehabilitation, but making good progress, feeling better than expected. Perera adds that the type of cricket being played greatly influences the strategy, sometimes requiring an aggressive approach, while other times it's about protecting one's wicket.

PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raja is with Bazid Khan to inspect the pitch. Bazid sys that this looks more like the usual Rawalpindi, where the ball will skip onto the bat. Adds that there are cracks but not wide ones. Agrees with Shanaka that if there is dew, then bowlers will find it difficult. On the par total, Khan feels that Zimbabwe need to get a minimum of 170. Then, quickly adds that the side needs to get 20 over par to counter for the dew. Ends by saying that it is difficult ground to defend, so the best way is to bowl first here.

The captain of Zimbabwe, SIKANDAR RAZA, says that Zimbabwe didn't score much runs in the previous match which pushed them onto the back foot, but stresses that today, they have come prepared. Raza further explains that each team member has a specific role to play. He reveals that initially, he was slated to bat at number 3 in the previous game but the side lost a wicket at a crucial juncture. Consequently, he was set to bat at number 4, but when he saw the left-arm spinner being brought on, he thought it wise to bat alongside a right-handed partner to create a left-right combination, thereby explaining that the batting order is flexible.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, DASUN SHANAKA, says that it is used pitch but he is choosing to field due to the expectations of dew later on in the evening. Adds that there are a few players from this squad who featured in the ODIs, so their experience in these conditions would be useful. On the plans for this match, Shanaka smiles and says that those would be to try and restrict Zimbabwe to as low a total as possible and cheekily adds that those would also include the wicket of Sikandar Raza!

Zimbabwe (Unchanged Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Tadiwanashe Marumani, Brendan Taylor (WK), Ryan Burl, Sikandar Raza (C), Tony Munyonga, Tashinga Musekiwa, Brad Evans, Tinotenda Maposa, Richard Ngarava and Graeme Cremer.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Dasun Shanaka (C), Kamindu Mendis, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Maheesh Theekshana, Nuwan Thushara and Eshan Malinga.
TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the toss and they have decided to BOWL first.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, are set to open their campaign in this tri-series. After their Asia Cup sojourn, they were completely outwashed by Pakistan in three match ODI series. But this is completely a different format, so we might expect them to make a comeback from their remorse. Their openers, Pathum Nissanka and Kamil Mishara, will look forward to provide a dream start to their side and the middle order will look forward to build on that start. But the bowling department needs to put on some extra effort. They didn't perform up to the mark in their previous series despite having spin wizard Wanindu Hasaranga and the likes of Dushmantha Chameera. Sri Lanka will aim to stamp their authority early and lay down a marker in their first appearance of the tournament. So, which team are you supporting? Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Zimbabwe come into this fixture with a loss after facing Pakistan in the opening game of this tri-series. The Chevrons' bowlers showed discipline against Pakistan, while their top order displayed flashes of promise. The team will once again look to their in-form performers like Sikandar Raza, who continues to shine with both bat and ball from his recent international outings, and Brad Evans, whose rhythm with the ball has been a huge positive. If their middle order can complement the good starts, Zimbabwe could push Sri Lanka hard.

Hello and a very warm welcome to all the cricket fans joining us for the second exciting clash in the 2025 T20 Tri-Series in Pakistan, where Sri Lanka take on Zimbabwe in what promises to be a high tempo contest. With Pakistan having edged the Chevrons in a tense finish in their previous encounter, the series has already shown its competitive edge, setting the perfect stage for today’s matchup.
... MATCHDAY ...

Highways are the arteries of a nation's infrastructure, driving economic mobility and progress. But in cricket, when we talk about highways, one name instantly dominates the conversation. Rawalpindi. And no, we're not joking. Experts and cricketing pundits have branded it so for years. While the tag might be debated, the 'Pindi wicket has earned its reputation as one of the flattest, most batting-friendly surfaces in world cricket. Yet here's the beautiful paradox. This very highway produced some of the most fearsome fast bowlers the game has ever seen. Shoaib Akhtar, the Rawalpindi Express himself, and the crafty Sohail Tanvir didn't just thrive here. These blokes made life difficult for the batters in the hay every now and then, forging with the batter’s egos at times, with their sheer pace and velocity generation. Ahh! Nostalgia kicking in. But nostalgia aside, the landscape has shifted. What we're witnessing now is a whole new pool of explosive talent armed with modern power-hitting, fearless intent, and the audacity to dismantle any bowling attack. Tri-series are still an intact part of the cricketing landscape. While they might not be frequent, it is great to see. Pakistan, the hosts, drew first blood in the series opener against the Chevrons in a rather dominating manner. And now, after a day’s break, Zimbabwe will be back in action against Sri Lanka, who will be playing their first-ever T20I at this venue. They faced a humbling ODI series defeat to Pakistan last week and will be desperate to make amends in the shorter format. But before the fireworks begin, Sri Lanka have been hit with disruption. Their original captain, Charith Asalanka and fast bowler Asitha Fernando have both been ruled out due to illness, forcing late changes to the squad. In Asalanka's absence, the armband returns to Dasun Shanaka, the former white-ball skipper who now finds himself thrust back into leadership with little time to settle. The reshuffle doesn't end there. Pavan Rathnayake has been drafted in as cover, while Vijayakanth Viyaskanth gets the nod with Wanindu Hasaranga still nursing the hamstring tightness that flared up during the ODI series. It's a patched-up Sri Lankan side walking into this tri-series. Apart from these changes, the squad is more or less the same. Three frontline pacers led by the speedy Dushmantha Chameera, and accompanied by the slingy Nuwan Thushara, along with Eshan Malinga, whereas Maheesh Theekshana will spearhead whatever spin is at their disposal. But Sri Lanka's real weapon? Their top order. Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka have been in solid touch this year, providing the kind of explosive starts that set platforms and demoralise attacks. Both are expected to shoulder the scoring burden upfront, especially with the middle order needing stability. On the other side of the camp, Zimbabwe might just be the most overworked team in world cricket right now. They've been on a relentless grind, hopping from series to series, format to format, with barely any time to breathe. But that exposure will only sharpen them. Sure, they lost to a full-strength Pakistan in the series opener, but as the cliche goes, there are always positives to squeeze out. And Zimbabwe have plenty. The opening pair of Brian Bennett and Tadiwanashe Marumani provided a solid launchpad, attacking with intent and setting the tone. The problem? The middle order crumbled. Sikandar Raza has been carrying the load almost single-handedly, but it's high time the rest step up and own their roles. On the bowling front, there's real promise. Brad Evans and Graeme Cremer were relentless in the Powerplay, while Richard Ngarava added bite. If Zimbabwe can get their middle order firing and maintain that early aggression with the ball, they're dangerous. These two teams met recently in a T20I series in Harare, which was won by the Lankans 2-1. But given the experience of playing four matches out of ten overall T20Is played at Rawalpindi, the Chevrons just might know a thing or two more about the deck. Can they spring a surprise and beat a patched-up Lankan side? Another delicious contest is up on the cards.
